What change is noticed in the shape of a pencil that is half immersed in water as shown in the Figure? Explain with a ray diagram. Write the name of the process associated with this observation. Ans:- The pencil appears bent because light from the part of the pencil under water is refracted at the water surface; the rays bend away from the normal when they pass from water to air, so the eye sees them as if they come from a point higher than the true tip. This process is called refraction (and the observed shift is often described as apparent depth).
13. When a light ray passes from water to air, the angle of incidence and angle of refraction formed at the water-air
separation layer are 40.5° and 60° respectively. Draw a ray diagram showing the
refraction and write the reason why an object outside appears to be farther away
from its actual position when it is viewed by an observer inside the water.
Ans:- When light travels from water (denser medium) to air (rarer medium), it
bends away from the normal. Because of this bending, the refracted rays entering
the observer’s eye appear to come from a point farther from the surface than the
actual object.
The object outside seems farther away because the refracted rays are extended
backward and form a virtual image that lies farther from the real position.
